findings.issue_text: Server-side duplicate-guest protection missing within a single request: incoming guests array is not deduped, so submitting duplicate emails creates two identical attendee rows via createMany and both receive emails; uniqueness check only exists in client-side schema
Existing-attendee filter is case-sensitive (guest === attendee.email), so 'A@X.com' bypasses existing 'a@x.com' and creates a duplicate
Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||, so team admins are denied FORBIDDEN even though they should be allowed; effective result is team-owner-only access
Fallback teamId ?? 0 in the isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner calls is an accidental sentinel that makes the team branch meaningless for non-team (personal) bookings

No check on booking.status: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, causing attendee creation, calendar updates, and iCal REQUEST emails with status CONFIRMED that effectively resurrect cancelled meetings
Blacklisted-guest check is case-sensitive and untrimmed: guest email is used raw against lowercased blacklist entries and env split doesn't trim, so 'Spam@X.com' and ' b@x.com' bypass the blacklist
Unbounded guests array (z.array with no .max()) allows authenticated attendees to submit thousands of emails in one call, enabling a mass-email/spam amplification vector
Email-send failure silently swallowed with bare console.log (no error object), handler returns success and UI toasts success while new guests are never notified

Attendee-initiated adds use the actor's calendar credentials instead of the organizer's: if the attendee has no credentials the calendar update silently no-ops, and if they do the update targets the wrong account
Exception in updateCalendarAttendees propagates after attendees were already persisted, leaving inconsistent state where the UI shows an error but the DB change has landed
Client: isInvalidEmail is never reset on successful add or dialog close, so a stale validation error banner shows on reopen
Client: closing via overlay/Esc (onOpenChange) does not reset multiEmailValue, so previously typed possibly-invalid emails reappear on reopen
Client: handleAdd returns silently when multiEmailValue is empty (all rows removed), leaving an unresponsive-looking Add button
Client error toast: message is never falsy, so when err.data is undefined the toast renders 'undefined: ...' and the || t('unable_to_add_guests') fallback is dead code

New/old guest email classification in email-manager.ts is case-sensitive: newGuests.includes(attendee.email) compares raw input against stored emails, potentially mis-classifying who receives the booking-confirmation vs notification email

Any booking attendee can add arbitrary guests to a booking because the permission check grants access to isAttendee, allowing attendees to mutate bookings, spam emails, and trigger calendar updates — the isAttendee branch should not exist if the feature is organizer/host-side
Unbounded guests array with no max-length in ZAddGuestsInputSchema allows an attendee to fan out emails/calendar updates to thousands of addresses in a single request
Guest blacklist check is case-sensitive because guest emails are not lowercased/normalized before comparison, allowing blacklist bypass with case variations
Existing-attendee duplicate check is case-sensitive, so the same email can be added repeatedly with case variations, generating duplicate emails/calendar updates
Server-side schema does not enforce uniqueness of the guests array (client-side .refine only), so direct API calls can insert duplicate attendee rows
isTeamAdminOrOwner check uses && instead of ||, requiring users to be both admin and owner, which breaks guest-adding for team admins
Seat-capacity is never enforced — attendees are created via raw prisma.booking.update regardless of remaining seatsPerTimeSlot, allowing seated bookings to be overfilled
No check of booking.status, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, sending CONFIRMED iCalendar REQUEST emails for cancelled meetings
Guests added via attendee rows instead of BookingSeat records for seated bookings, which may desync seat-based features like attendee visibility and per-seat data

EventManager is built with the calling user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)), so calendar attendee updates are attempted with credentials that don't own the target calendar event when the caller is an attendee or team admin
Crash path when booking.userId is null: where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } causes findFirstOrThrow to throw a raw Prisma error surfaced as a 500 instead of a handled TRPC error
Unbounded guests array in addGuests.schema.ts with no .max() limit allows mass DB writes, email fan-out, and calendar API calls in a single request, enabling resource exhaustion and email spam

sendAddGuestsEmails sends emails to all attendees (existing + new) plus organizer and team members on every invocation, awaited synchronously in the request path, causing response latency to grow linearly with attendee count and quadratic total email volume

Dedupe filter uses exact-match comparison (guest === attendee.email) without case normalization, allowing duplicate attendee rows (e.g., User@Example.com vs user@example.com) that compound email and calendar work over time
utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate() with no input invalidates every query under the bookings router, forcing refetch of all active booking lists after adding a single guest
`&&` should be `||` in the isTeamAdminOrOwner check (addGuests.handler.ts:52-54); requiring both admin and owner means team admins are incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN errors
Blacklisted guest emails can be bypassed via case variation because the incoming guest value is compared without lowercasing against the lowercased blacklist (addGuests.handler.ts:67-77)

No server-side deduplication of guests within a single request; ZAddGuestsInputSchema lacks a uniqueness refinement and the handler only dedupes against existing attendees, allowing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails (addGuests.schema.ts:4-6, addGuests.handler.ts:71-78)

Case-sensitive duplicate check against existing attendees (guest === attendee.email) creates duplicate attendee rows for emails differing only in case, and sendAddGuestsEmails' newGuests.includes(attendee.email) also misses the case mismatch causing wrong email template classification (addGuests.handler.ts:71-74, email-manager.ts:538-543)

No booking status check before adding guests, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings, triggering calendar updates and misleading 'CONFIRMED' ics REQUEST emails for events that no longer exist (addGuests.handler.ts:28-37)

Seated bookings: seatsPerTimeSlot is never enforced (no capacity check) and BookingSeat records are not created, bypassing seat accounting and desynchronizing attendee counts (addGuests.handler.ts:71-90, 150-151)

Bookings without a userId cause prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with id: 0 to throw a raw PrismaClientNotFoundError surfacing as an unhandled 500 instead of a typed TRPCError with a translatable message (addGuests.handler.ts:59-67)
Mutation response returns a hardcoded, non-localized English string 'Guests added' (addGuests.handler.ts:174) instead of an i18n key, inconsistent with sibling mutations and leaking untranslated text

Email-send failures are swallowed with a console.log, so the user sees 'Guests added' success when emails were never sent and calendars/attendees are out of sync; failure should be logged with the error object and surfaced in the response contract (addGuests.handler.ts:165-168)

Unbounded guests array size on the input schema — no .max() on z.array(z.string().email()), allowing a single authenticated request to create arbitrary attendees and fan out emails and calendar writes (addGuests.schema.ts:5)

isInvalidEmail error banner is never reset on successful submit or dialog reopen, so the warning banner reappears when the dialog is next opened after a prior failed attempt (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:53-62, 96-102)
Authorization check uses && instead of || in isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner check, wrongly denying team admins who aren't owners (FORBIDDEN error on normal-usage path)
Email failure is silently swallowed: catch block logs only a static message, discarding the error object with no stack/message, retry, queue, or user-facing signal

Non-atomic multi-step write: DB update commits before calendar/email steps; if updateCalendarAttendees throws, guests are already persisted with no rollback or compensation, leaving inconsistent state
updateCalendarAttendees runs with the requesting user's credentials via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) instead of the organizer's, likely failing when an attendee adds guests

Case-sensitivity breaks duplicate suppression and guest blacklist: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but guests are not, and duplicate detection is case-sensitive, allowing blacklist bypass and duplicate attendee rows
No booking-state validation: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings, sending ICS emails that resurrect cancelled events on guests' calendars
Unbounded guest list with no cap, rate limiting, or batching allows any attendee to trigger email fan-out to thousands of addresses in one request
findFirstOrThrow with where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } throws an unhandled Prisma P2025 error (500) when booking.userId is null instead of a clean TRPCError
Error toast fallback is dead code: the message template is always truthy so the || t('unable_to_add_guests') fallback never fires, and t() on a non-translation-key renders the raw key string
Validation-error banner (isInvalidEmail) is never reset on subsequent successful validation, so the warning persists after the user fixes the emails
Authorization logic uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner, requiring users to be both admin and owner, silently denying team admins from managing bookings
Server-side validation gap: input array is not deduped or case-normalized, so User@Example.com vs user@example.com creates duplicate attendee rows
Handler compares existing attendees case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email), allowing duplicate attendees differing only in case
No dedupe within the guests array in the server schema; the uniqueness Zod refine exists only in the client component
blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but the guest email is not, so Spam@X.com bypasses the blacklist check
Client duplicates the server Zod schema inline in AddGuestsDialog instead of sharing the server schema, and the copies have already diverged (client adds uniqueness refine)
Inline Zod schema in AddGuestsDialog is recreated every render
~50 lines of booking-to-CalendarEvent mapping duplicated from sibling handlers (editLocation.handler/confirm.handler); should be extracted into a shared bookingToCalendarEvent helper
EventManager is built with the caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so calendar attendee updates likely fail silently when non-owners (attendees/admins) add guests
Email send errors are swallowed: err is discarded, console.log is used instead of the codebase logger, and no booking/user context is provided
Validation error state (isInvalidEmail) is only cleared on cancel, not on success or dialog close, so the stale error reappears next time the dialog opens
findFirstOrThrow uses a magic 0 sentinel (booking.userId || 0) causing an unhandled Prisma NotFoundError (raw 500) instead of a clean TRPCError NOT_FOUND like the earlier booking fetch
Hardcoded untranslated string 'Remove email' in the locale-agnostic packages/ui MultiEmail component, despite the component already using useLocale for other strings
Blacklisted guest email check is bypassed via case mismatch: blacklist entries are lowercased but the guest email is compared verbatim, so 'SPAM@evil.com' bypasses 'spam@evil.com'

EventManager is built from the acting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so updateCalendarAttendees may silently no-op or fail for the organizer's calendar while the DB update and success response still occur
No validation of booking.status, allowing guests to be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings, which then receive ICS attachments with method: 'REQUEST' and status: 'CONFIRMED' for cancelled events
isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so only team owners pass the permission check and legitimate team admins are denied with permission errors
Attendees can add an unlimited number of arbitrary guests with no rate limiting or cap on guest count, enabling email spam/spoofing from the organizer's identity via replyTo

TOCTOU race between the dedup check and prisma createMany allows concurrent requests to insert duplicate attendee rows, and the dedup comparison is case-sensitive so 'User@X.com' vs 'user@x.com' produces duplicates; no DB unique constraint on (bookingId, email)
Email send failures are swallowed with console.log and the error object is discarded, so the mutation returns 'Guests added' success even when no guest was notified or ICS invite sent
Seated bookings: no capacity check before inserting attendees and no bookingSeat records are created, allowing overbooking and divergence from seats-flow logic

Partial-failure ordering: DB write happens before updateCalendarAttendees with no rollback, so a calendar failure persists guests but returns an error, and retrying hits the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' BAD_REQUEST because uniqueGuests.length is 0
prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) throws a raw Prisma 500 error instead of a handled TRPCError when booking.userId is null
No guard against adding guests to past events, since there is no startTime check, resulting in CONFIRMED invites being sent for meetings that already happened

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side duplicate-guest protection missing within a single request: incoming guests array is not deduped, so submitting duplicate emails creates two identical attendee rows via createMany and both receive emails; uniqueness check only exists in client-side schema
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying issue: the server does not deduplicate duplicate emails within the incoming guests list, so createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows when the client submits repeated emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing-attendee filter is case-sensitive (guest === attendee.email), so 'A@X.com' bypasses existing 'a@x.com' and creates a duplicate

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, existing attendees are filtered with a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` when computing `uniqueGuests`. Since incoming `guests` are not normalized (e.g., `toLowerCase()`), an email like `A@x.com` will not match an existing attendee stored as `a@x.com`, allowing a duplicate attendee to be created via `attendees.createMany`. The blacklist check lowercases only the blacklist entries, not `guest`, reinforcing the lack of normalization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||, so team admins are denied FORBIDDEN even though they should be allowed; effective result is team-owner-only access
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same logical error in the permission check: using && requires both admin and owner, whereas it should be || to allow either role. It also correctly notes the consequence (admins wrongly forbidden, owner-only access).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fallback teamId ?? 0 in the isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner calls is an accidental sentinel that makes the team branch meaningless for non-team (personal) bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, permission logic computes `isTeamAdminOrOwner` as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. For non-team bookings where `booking.eventType?.teamId` is `undefined`, this will always check team id `0`, which effectively makes the “team admin/owner” branch irrelevant for personal bookings and may trigger unnecessary DB checks (and depends on how `isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner` handle `0`). The diff doesn’t prove it causes incorrect authorization, since organizers/attendees are still allowed via the other checks, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded logic/clarity concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check on booking.status: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, causing attendee creation, calendar updates, and iCal REQUEST emails with status CONFIRMED that effectively resurrect cancelled meetings

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` there is no guard on the booking lifecycle/state (e.g., `booking.status`). The handler will update DB attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and send emails. The new email templates always generate an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`generateIcsString({ ..., status: "CONFIRMED" })` in both `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`). So if this mutation is invoked for a cancelled/rejected booking, it can create attendees, update calendars, and send CONFIRMED iCal REQUESTs, potentially reactivating a cancelled meeting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklisted-guest check is case-sensitive and untrimmed: guest email is used raw against lowercased blacklist entries and env split doesn't trim, so 'Spam@X.com' and ' b@x.com' bypass the blacklist
Unbounded guests array (z.array with no .max()) allows authenticated attendees to submit thousands of emails in one call, enabling a mass-email/spam amplification vector

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC mutation `addGuests` accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`). The UI (`MultiEmail`) allows adding arbitrary additional fields (pushes `""` each time) and the handler persists them via `createMany` and then triggers email sending via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (which `Promise.all`s over attendees) in `addGuests.handler.ts`. Because the permission check allows any authenticated attendee of the booking (`isAttendee`) to call this endpoint, an attendee could submit a very large array and cause bulk DB writes and bulk outbound emails, creating a spam/amplification vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-send failure silently swallowed with bare console.log (no error object), handler returns success and UI toasts success while new guests are never notified

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` (no `err`), and then execution continues to `return { message: "Guests added" }`. The UI (`AddGuestsDialog`) shows a success toast on TRPC `onSuccess`, so if email sending fails, the mutation still reports success and users will be told “Guests added” even though notifications were not sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee-initiated adds use the actor's calendar credentials instead of the organizer's: if the attendee has no credentials the calendar update silently no-ops, and if they do the update targets the wrong account

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. This uses the *actor* (`ctx.user`) credentials to update the booking’s calendar attendees, even though the booking’s organizer (and their credentials are available via the earlier `booking.user` include / separate `organizer` lookup) is likely the owner of the destination calendar. If an attendee (authorized by `isAttendee`) triggers this mutation, the update will run under the attendee’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, which can fail to update the organizer’s calendar or update the wrong account.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Exception in updateCalendarAttendees propagates after attendees were already persisted, leaving inconsistent state where the UI shows an error but the DB change has landed

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new attendees are persisted first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and only afterward `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is awaited without any try/catch or transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the TRPC mutation will error (UI shows failure) even though the DB change already landed, leaving the system in an inconsistent state as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client: isInvalidEmail is never reset on successful add or dialog close, so a stale validation error banner shows on reopen

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure in `handleAdd()`, but it is not reset in the mutation `onSuccess` handler (which only calls `setIsOpenDialog(false)` and `setMultiEmailValue([""])`). Because the dialog component remains mounted and the banner is gated solely on `isInvalidEmail`, reopening the dialog after a successful add can still show the stale error banner. It is only reset on the Cancel button path, and not when closing via success or `onOpenChange`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client: closing via overlay/Esc (onOpenChange) does not reset multiEmailValue, so previously typed possibly-invalid emails reappear on reopen

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `Dialog` is controlled via `open={isOpenDialog}` and `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`. State cleanup (`setMultiEmailValue([""])`, `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`) only happens on the Cancel button click and on mutation success, not when the dialog is closed by clicking the overlay or pressing Esc (which triggers `onOpenChange` directly). Therefore previously entered (possibly invalid) emails and `isInvalidEmail` can persist and reappear when reopened.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client: handleAdd returns silently when multiEmailValue is empty (all rows removed), leaving an unresponsive-looking Add button

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.handleAdd`, when `multiEmailValue.length === 0` it `return`s without any feedback or disabling the Add button. This state is reachable because `MultiEmail` allows removing rows via `onClickAddon` (splicing the array), which can leave `value` as `[]`. The dialog footer Add button remains clickable but does nothing, matching the finding’s “unresponsive-looking Add button”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client error toast: message is never falsy, so when err.data is undefined the toast renders 'undefined: ...' and the || t('unable_to_add_guests') fallback is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the onError handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. Because this is a template literal, `message` is always a (non-empty) string; when `err.data?.code` is undefined it becomes the literal text `"undefined: ..."`, so the fallback `t("unable_to_add_guests")` is effectively dead and the UI can show `undefined:` to users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New/old guest email classification in email-manager.ts is case-sensitive: newGuests.includes(attendee.email) compares raw input against stored emails, potentially mis-classifying who receives the booking-confirmation vs notification email

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts), the logic `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` is a strict, case-sensitive string comparison. `newGuests` comes from user input (`guests` in `addGuests.handler.ts`) and is not normalized (no lowercasing), and attendee emails (`calendarEvent.attendees`) come from DB values which may have different casing. This can misclassify an email as “not a new guest,” sending `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` instead of `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (or vice versa). The diff shows no normalization on either side, so the issue is real and introduced/exposed by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any booking attendee can add arbitrary guests to a booking because the permission check grants access to isAttendee, allowing attendees to mutate bookings, spam emails, and trigger calendar updates — the isAttendee branch should not exist if the feature is organizer/host-side

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the authorization explicitly allows any existing attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the guard is `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`. That means a logged-in attendee (not just the organizer/admin) can call `viewer.bookings.addGuests`, which will (a) mutate booking attendees in Prisma, (b) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and (c) send emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, enabling unwanted calendar/email side effects. This matches the finding that attendees can mutate the booking and trigger spam/updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded guests array with no max-length in ZAddGuestsInputSchema allows an attendee to fan out emails/calendar updates to thousands of addresses in a single request

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `addGuests` with `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defined as `{ bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email()) }` (no `.max()`), and the handler `addGuestsHandler` directly uses this array to `createMany` attendees, call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which does a `Promise.all` fan-out over attendees/team members. With no bound in the schema or handler, a caller can submit an extremely large `guests` array in one request, causing large DB writes and mass email/calendar update fan-out (abuse/DoS/spam vector).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guest blacklist check is case-sensitive because guest emails are not lowercased/normalized before comparison, allowing blacklist bypass with case variations
Existing-attendee duplicate check is case-sensitive, so the same email can be added repeatedly with case variations, generating duplicate emails/calendar updates

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the existing-attendee duplicate filter is case-sensitive: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and the blacklist check is also case-sensitive: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, even though the blacklist is lowercased. Since neither the backend schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema` just validates `.email()`) nor the frontend uniqueness refine normalizes case, an email already present as `test@example.com` can be added again as `Test@example.com`, creating duplicate attendee records and triggering extra calendar/email updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side schema does not enforce uniqueness of the guests array (client-side .refine only), so direct API calls can insert duplicate attendee rows

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.schema.ts`, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` (no uniqueness constraint). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering against existing `booking.attendees` and a blacklist, but it does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. Therefore a direct API call like `guests: ["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]` would leave both entries in `uniqueGuests` and `createMany` would attempt to insert duplicate attendee rows for the same booking (or potentially trigger a DB constraint error if one exists). The client-side `.refine` in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` does not protect the API.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner check uses && instead of ||, requiring users to be both admin and owner, which breaks guest-adding for team admins

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`, meaning the user must be both admin and owner to pass (`const isTeamAdminOrOwner = ... && ...`). The subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` will therefore block team admins who are not also owners, contradicting the variable name and likely intended access rule (admin OR owner).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Seat-capacity is never enforced — attendees are created via raw prisma.booking.update regardless of remaining seatsPerTimeSlot, allowing seated bookings to be overfilled

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the code unconditionally adds new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}})` without checking `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or current attendee count / remaining seats). The handler even propagates `seatsPerTimeSlot` into the `CalendarEvent` (`evt.seatsPerTimeSlot = booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`), indicating seat limits are relevant, but no enforcement occurs before inserting attendees. This allows adding guests to an already-full seated booking, overfilling capacity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check of booking.status, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, sending CONFIRMED iCalendar REQUEST emails for cancelled meetings

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the booking is fetched via `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId }, include: ... })` and then guests are added and calendar/email updates are performed with no check of any booking lifecycle field (e.g., cancelled/rejected status). The new email templates explicitly generate ICS payloads with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` (`packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`), so if a cancelled booking is passed in, the handler would still update attendees and send CONFIRMED meeting requests, which is incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guests added via attendee rows instead of BookingSeat records for seated bookings, which may desync seat-based features like attendee visibility and per-seat data

adjudication.rationale: The new addGuests flow persists guests by creating BookingAttendee rows only (prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}}) in addGuests.handler.ts) and does not reference any seat/BookingSeat model or per-seat assignment logic. The diff also surfaces seat-related fields on the CalendarEvent (seatsPerTimeSlot, seatsShowAttendees), suggesting seated-booking semantics exist, but this mutation does not appear to account for them. Whether this is a true defect depends on how the rest of the system models seated bookings (not shown in the diff), so it’s best classified as a scoped architectural/edge-case concern grounded in the added code rather than a verifiable broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built with the calling user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)), so calendar attendee updates are attempted with credentials that don't own the target calendar event when the caller is an attendee or team admin

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to call it (it permits `isAttendee` and a computed `isTeamAdminOrOwner`). However, the calendar update is performed by constructing `EventManager` with the *calling* user (`ctx.user`) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and then calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. If the caller is an attendee or a team admin (not the booking organizer), those credentials may not own/have access to the organizer’s destination calendar event referenced by `booking`/`destinationCalendar`, so the attendee update attempt can fail or act on the wrong account. This behavior is directly shown by `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); ... new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] });` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Crash path when booking.userId is null: where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } causes findFirstOrThrow to throw a raw Prisma error surfaced as a 500 instead of a handled TRPC error

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuestsHandler`, organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined`, this coerces to `0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (not wrapped in a `TRPCError`), likely surfacing as an unhandled 500 rather than a controlled TRPC error. This crash path is present in the diff and introduced with the new handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded guests array in addGuests.schema.ts with no .max() limit allows mass DB writes, email fan-out, and calendar API calls in a single request, enabling resource exhaustion and email spam

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound. The handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`) then performs potentially expensive operations proportional to that array size: `attendees.createMany` DB writes, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` calendar API updates, and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which fan-outs emails over attendees/team members. With no `.max()` limit, a single request can trigger large DB/calendar/email workloads, enabling resource exhaustion/spam.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails sends emails to all attendees (existing + new) plus organizer and team members on every invocation, awaited synchronously in the request path, causing response latency to grow linearly with attendee count and quadratic total email volume

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` builds `emailsToSend` for the organizer, each team member, and **every** attendee (`...calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`), and in `addGuests.handler.ts` it is awaited on the request path (`await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`). This makes request latency scale with attendee/team size and performs potentially large fan-out work inline. The "quadratic total email volume" part is not directly verifiable from the diff (it depends on how often the mutation is invoked over time), but the synchronous fan-out to all attendees is clearly present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dedupe filter uses exact-match comparison (guest === attendee.email) without case normalization, allowing duplicate attendee rows (e.g., User@Example.com vs user@example.com) that compound email and calendar work over time

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the dedupe logic for new guests is `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and blacklist check is `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing `guest`/`attendee.email` casing. Since the input schema (`z.string().email()`) does not lowercase, this can treat `User@Example.com` and `user@example.com` as different and allow duplicate attendee creation via `createMany`, leading to compounded calendar/email updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate() with no input invalidates every query under the bookings router, forcing refetch of all active booking lists after adding a single guest

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the mutation `onSuccess` calls `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` with no args. In tRPC/React Query utils, invalidating a router path without specifying a procedure/input will invalidate all cached queries under `viewer.bookings`, potentially refetching multiple active booking lists even though only one booking (`bookingId`) changed. This is a concrete performance/scope concern grounded in the diff, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `&&` should be `||` in the isTeamAdminOrOwner check (addGuests.handler.ts:52-54); requiring both admin and owner means team admins are incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN errors

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. The subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` will therefore reject users who are admins but not owners (a common role split). Using `||` would match the intent implied by the variable name and allow either role.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklisted guest emails can be bypassed via case variation because the incoming guest value is compared without lowercasing against the lowercased blacklist (addGuests.handler.ts:67-77)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, blacklistedGuestEmails is normalized to lowercase (split + toLowerCase), but the incoming guest string is compared directly via `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`. This allows bypassing the blacklist by submitting the same email with different casing (e.g., `Test@Example.com` vs `test@example.com`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side deduplication of guests within a single request; ZAddGuestsInputSchema lacks a uniqueness refinement and the handler only dedupes against existing attendees, allowing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails (addGuests.schema.ts:4-6, addGuests.handler.ts:71-78)

adjudication.rationale: Verified: server input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness refinement (addGuests.schema.ts). In the handler, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but does not deduplicate duplicates within the `guests` array itself (addGuests.handler.ts: `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`). If the request contains the same new email twice, both entries pass the filter and are inserted via `attendees.createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows/emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive duplicate check against existing attendees (guest === attendee.email) creates duplicate attendee rows for emails differing only in case, and sendAddGuestsEmails' newGuests.includes(attendee.email) also misses the case mismatch causing wrong email template classification (addGuests.handler.ts:71-74, email-manager.ts:538-543)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, uniqueGuests is computed with strict, case-sensitive comparisons: `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (guest is not lowercased while blacklist entries are), so emails differing only by case can bypass both checks and be inserted via `createMany`, producing duplicate attendee rows and potentially bypassing the blacklist. In email-manager.ts `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` which is also case-sensitive, so a case mismatch will cause the wrong template branch to be chosen.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking status check before adding guests, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings, triggering calendar updates and misleading 'CONFIRMED' ics REQUEST emails for events that no longer exist (addGuests.handler.ts:28-37)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking and proceeds to update DB attendees (`prisma.booking.update`), call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and send emails, but there is no conditional check on any booking lifecycle/status (e.g., cancelled/rejected/pending) before doing so. The newly added email templates (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts` / `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) also always generate an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"`, so if this mutation is invoked on a non-active booking record it would still trigger calendar updates and send misleading confirmed invites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Seated bookings: seatsPerTimeSlot is never enforced (no capacity check) and BookingSeat records are not created, bypassing seat accounting and desynchronizing attendee counts (addGuests.handler.ts:71-90, 150-151)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new guests are added via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` with no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (the value is only copied into the `CalendarEvent` at the end). There is also no creation/update of any seat-accounting records (e.g., `BookingSeat`) in this handler—only `attendees` are modified—so for seated events this can exceed capacity and desynchronize seat counts vs attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Bookings without a userId cause prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with id: 0 to throw a raw PrismaClientNotFoundError surfacing as an unhandled 500 instead of a typed TRPCError with a translatable message (addGuests.handler.ts:59-67)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is null/undefined, this queries `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (Prisma not-found). There’s no surrounding try/catch converting this into a `TRPCError`, so it will bubble up as an internal/untyped error rather than a translatable TRPC error message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mutation response returns a hardcoded, non-localized English string 'Guests added' (addGuests.handler.ts:174) instead of an i18n key, inconsistent with sibling mutations and leaking untranslated text

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the mutation returns a hardcoded English payload `return { message: "Guests added" };` (end of file). The UI shown in this diff does not use this response text (it toasts `t("guests_added")` on success), so it’s not a functional breakage, but it is a real, diff-grounded consistency/i18n concern compared to other server errors that return i18n keys (e.g., `booking_not_found`, `emails_must_be_unique_valid`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-send failures are swallowed with a console.log, so the user sees 'Guests added' success when emails were never sent and calendars/attendees are out of sync; failure should be logged with the error object and surfaced in the response contract (addGuests.handler.ts:165-168)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and then proceeds to return `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the mutation reports success even if `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` fails, and the error context is lost (no `err` logged). However, the diff shows calendar attendee updates happen *before* the email try/catch (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)`), so the claim that calendars/attendees become out of sync due to email failure is not directly supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded guests array size on the input schema — no .max() on z.array(z.string().email()), allowing a single authenticated request to create arbitrary attendees and fan out emails and calendar writes (addGuests.schema.ts:5)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` with `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` and no bound (`.max(...)`) (addGuests.schema.ts:5). The new `addGuestsHandler` then uses `createMany` to insert all provided guests and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` plus `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which can fan out emails/ICS updates to many recipients. With only authentication required, a single request could supply an arbitrarily large array and trigger excessive DB writes and outbound email/calendar operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail error banner is never reset on successful submit or dialog reopen, so the warning banner reappears when the dialog is next opened after a prior failed attempt (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:53-62, 96-102)

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure in `handleAdd`, but it is never reset in the mutation `onSuccess` handler (only `setIsOpenDialog(false)` and `setMultiEmailValue([""])` are called). Since the dialog component is always mounted (rendered in `BookingListItem`), reopening it after a successful submit can still show the error banner because `isInvalidEmail` remains `true` unless the user hit Cancel (which does reset it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization check uses && instead of || in isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner check, wrongly denying team admins who aren't owners (FORBIDDEN error on normal-usage path)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. That contradicts the variable name and typical authorization intent (admin OR owner) and will incorrectly reject legitimate team admins who are not owners, triggering the subsequent `FORBIDDEN` path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failure is silently swallowed: catch block logs only a static message, discarding the error object with no stack/message, retry, queue, or user-facing signal

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which discards the caught `err` and always returns success (`{ message: "Guests added" }`). This is a concrete observability/robustness issue introduced by the diff: failures to send emails are not surfaced to the caller and the logged message omits the error/stack, making troubleshooting difficult.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic multi-step write: DB update commits before calendar/email steps; if updateCalendarAttendees throws, guests are already persisted with no rollback or compensation, leaving inconsistent state

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` before performing external side effects (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`). There is no transaction or compensation logic; `updateCalendarAttendees` is not wrapped in a try/catch, so if it throws, the mutation fails but the DB write has already committed, leaving booking attendees updated while calendar updates/emails may not have occurred.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateCalendarAttendees runs with the requesting user's credentials via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) instead of the organizer's, likely failing when an attendee adds guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, non-organizers are allowed to add guests (`isAttendee` check), but the calendar update is performed using the requesting user's credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, where `user` is `ctx.user` (the requester). If an attendee (not the organizer) triggers this mutation, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will likely lack the organizer's calendar credentials and fail to update the booking's calendar attendees, despite the handler proceeding. The diff shows organizer data is fetched but not used for credentials/EventManager.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitivity breaks duplicate suppression and guest blacklist: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but guests are not, and duplicate detection is case-sensitive, allowing blacklist bypass and duplicate attendee rows

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but the incoming `guests` values are not lowercased before checking `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, so a guest like `Bad@Example.com` can bypass a lowercase blacklist entry. Likewise, duplicate suppression against existing attendees is `guest === attendee.email` (case-sensitive), allowing the same mailbox with different casing to be added as a new attendee row. The UI-side uniqueness refine in `AddGuestsDialog` also uses a `Set` on raw strings, which is case-sensitive as well.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking-state validation: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings, sending ICS emails that resurrect cancelled events on guests' calendars

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts), the booking is fetched by `id` and then guests are appended via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` with no checks on any booking lifecycle state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) or time bounds (e.g., `endTime` in the past). The subsequent side effects always run: `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. The new email templates also generate an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` (packages/emails/templates/*add-guests-email.ts). The finding’s exact claim about “cancelled/rejected” depends on fields not shown in the diff, but the lack of state/time validation before sending CONFIRMED REQUEST ICS is real and could cause unintended calendar updates for non-active bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded guest list with no cap, rate limiting, or batching allows any attendee to trigger email fan-out to thousands of addresses in one request

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no max length (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`), and the UI (`MultiEmail`) lets users add unlimited email fields. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, any booking attendee is authorized (`isAttendee`) to call it, and it triggers email fan-out via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which builds a `Promise.all` over all attendees plus organizer/team members (`packages/emails/email-manager.ts`). There is no cap, batching, or rate limiting shown, so a single request can attempt to email thousands of addresses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow with where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } throws an unhandled Prisma P2025 error (500) when booking.userId is null instead of a clean TRPCError

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts), the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } ... })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined`, this will query `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (Prisma P2025 / record not found). There is no surrounding error handling to convert this into a `TRPCError`, so it can surface as an internal error (500) rather than a clean TRPC error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error toast fallback is dead code: the message template is always truthy so the || t('unable_to_add_guests') fallback never fires, and t() on a non-translation-key renders the raw key string

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` the `onError` handler builds `message` via a template literal: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;`. A template literal always returns a non-empty string (at minimum it includes `": "`), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never hit the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback and may display confusing strings like `"undefined: <...>"` when `err.data?.code` is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation-error banner (isInvalidEmail) is never reset on subsequent successful validation, so the warning persists after the user fixes the emails

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation (`handleAdd` else-branch), but it is never cleared when validation later succeeds. On subsequent clicks where `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` succeeds, the code calls `addGuestsMutation.mutate(...)` without `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`, so the red validation banner can remain visible even after the user fixes the emails (until the dialog is closed or Cancel is pressed, which explicitly resets it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner, requiring users to be both admin and owner, silently denying team admins from managing bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`, meaning a user must be both a team admin and a team owner to pass that check. Given the variable name and typical permission semantics, this will incorrectly deny access to team admins who are not owners, leading to unintended `FORBIDDEN` for admins attempting to add guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side validation gap: input array is not deduped or case-normalized, so User@Example.com vs user@example.com creates duplicate attendee rows

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with a filter that only checks against existing `booking.attendees` via strict equality (`guest === attendee.email`) and does not dedupe the `guests` input array itself or normalize case. This allows duplicates like `User@Example.com` vs `user@example.com` (or repeated identical entries) to pass through and be inserted via `attendees.createMany` (and the blacklist check also compares lowercased blacklist entries against non-lowercased `guest`). The server schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` also lacks uniqueness/case-normalization constraints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Handler compares existing attendees case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email), allowing duplicate attendees differing only in case

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed using a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and blacklist check `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guests` are not normalized (e.g., lowercased/trimmed) and attendee emails may differ only by case, the handler can create duplicate attendees like `Foo@bar.com` vs `foo@bar.com` and potentially bypass a lowercased blacklist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No dedupe within the guests array in the server schema; the uniqueness Zod refine exists only in the client component

adjudication.rationale: Verified: the server input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness, while the client dialog adds a uniqueness `refine` locally. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees/blacklist but does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array (it uses `guests.filter(...)` without a `Set`). So sending duplicate emails in one request can result in duplicate attendee rows via `attendees.createMany`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but the guest email is not, so Spam@X.com bypasses the blacklist check
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same case-sensitivity bug: the blacklist entries are lowercased but the input guest email is not, allowing uppercase variants (e.g., Spam@X.com) to bypass the includes() check. This matches the golden comment's underlying issue and impact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client duplicates the server Zod schema inline in AddGuestsDialog instead of sharing the server schema, and the copies have already diverged (client adds uniqueness refine)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the client defining an inline Zod schema in `AddGuestsDialog` (`const ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)`) to validate the guest email list, while the server defines its own input schema in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())`) with no uniqueness constraint. This is indeed duplicated validation logic across client/server and the two have already diverged (client enforces uniqueness; server schema does not), which is an architectural/consistency concern grounded in the diff rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inline Zod schema in AddGuestsDialog is recreated every render

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `const ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` is declared inside the `AddGuestsDialog` component body, so it will be re-created on every render. This is verifiable from the diff and is a performance/structure concern rather than a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ~50 lines of booking-to-CalendarEvent mapping duplicated from sibling handlers (editLocation.handler/confirm.handler); should be extracted into a shared bookingToCalendarEvent helper

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests.handler.ts` introduces a sizable manual `booking` → `CalendarEvent` construction (`const evt: CalendarEvent = { ... }` plus `videoCallData` handling) before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)`. Even though the diff doesn’t show `editLocation.handler`/`confirm.handler` to conclusively verify duplication across siblings, the diff does show new nontrivial mapping logic being added in this handler, which is a maintainability/architecture concern and a good candidate for extraction into a shared helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built with the caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so calendar attendee updates likely fail silently when non-owners (attendees/admins) add guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user`/`ctx.user` is the *caller* (could be an attendee or team admin). The booking owner’s/organizer’s credentials are never fetched/used (despite loading `booking.user` including `credentials`). As a result, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will attempt to update calendars using the caller’s credentials rather than the booking owner’s, which is incorrect for non-owner callers and can prevent attendee updates from being applied to the actual organizer’s connected calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send errors are swallowed: err is discarded, console.log is used instead of the codebase logger, and no booking/user context is provided

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. This discards `err`, uses `console.log` instead of any structured/codebase logger, and omits useful context (e.g., `bookingId`, organizer/user, guest list). The behavior is verifiably present in the diff; it’s primarily an observability/operational robustness issue rather than a definite correctness defect because the mutation still completes after updating attendees/calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation error state (isInvalidEmail) is only cleared on cancel, not on success or dialog close, so the stale error reappears next time the dialog opens

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation (`handleAdd`), but it is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button handler. On success, the dialog closes and `multiEmailValue` resets, but `isInvalidEmail` is not cleared (`onSuccess` only calls `setIsOpenDialog(false)` and `setMultiEmailValue([""])`). Since the component stays mounted and only `open` toggles, reopening the dialog can show the stale error state immediately.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow uses a magic 0 sentinel (booking.userId || 0) causing an unhandled Prisma NotFoundError (raw 500) instead of a clean TRPCError NOT_FOUND like the earlier booking fetch

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, organizer is loaded via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined`, this queries `id=0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma not-found error that is not converted to a `TRPCError`, unlike the earlier explicit `if (!booking) throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" ... })`. This can surface as an internal/500 error instead of a clean TRPC NOT_FOUND/handled error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded untranslated string 'Remove email' in the locale-agnostic packages/ui MultiEmail component, despite the component already using useLocale for other strings

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the tooltip uses a hardcoded string: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">`, while the same component already calls `useLocale()` and uses `t(...)` for other labels (e.g. `{t("add_another")}`). This is a real, diff-grounded i18n inconsistency, but it doesn't break functionality, so it's not a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklisted guest email check is bypassed via case mismatch: blacklist entries are lowercased but the guest email is compared verbatim, so 'SPAM@evil.com' bypasses 'spam@evil.com'

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is built with `.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`, but the filter checks `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where `guest` is used verbatim (not lowercased). This allows case-variant emails (e.g., `SPAM@evil.com`) to bypass a blacklist entry `spam@evil.com`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built from the acting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so updateCalendarAttendees may silently no-op or fail for the organizer's calendar while the DB update and success response still occur

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking attendees are persisted via `prisma.booking.update(...)`, then calendar updates are attempted with an `EventManager` constructed from the *acting* user: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. However, this mutation explicitly allows non-organizers (e.g., an attendee) to add guests (`isAttendee` check), and the booking’s organizer is `booking.userId` (fetched separately as `organizer`). In those cases, calendar updates for the organizer’s connected calendar can fail/no-op because the EventManager is not using the organizer’s credentials, while the DB update and success response still proceed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No validation of booking.status, allowing guests to be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings, which then receive ICS attachments with method: 'REQUEST' and status: 'CONFIRMED' for cancelled events

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` a booking is fetched and updated (`prisma.booking.findFirst` / `prisma.booking.update`) without any check on `booking.status` to prevent adding attendees to cancelled/rejected bookings. The new emails for this flow explicitly generate ICS payloads with `method: "REQUEST"` and `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`), so if the handler is called for a cancelled booking it would send confirmed REQUEST invites for an event that may no longer be valid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so only team owners pass the permission check and legitimate team admins are denied with permission errors

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. This will deny access to users who are team admins but not owners, causing the subsequent permission check (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`) to incorrectly reject legitimate admins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendees can add an unlimited number of arbitrary guests with no rate limiting or cap on guest count, enabling email spam/spoofing from the organizer's identity via replyTo

adjudication.rationale: The new addGuests flow accepts an unbounded `guests` array (ZAddGuestsInputSchema: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)`), and the UI (`MultiEmail` / `AddGuestsDialog`) allows adding arbitrary numbers of email fields with no cap. The server handler (`addGuestsHandler`) performs no rate limiting or guest-count limit and permits any attendee of the booking (`isAttendee`) to add guests, then sends emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. The email templates set headers that can make the email appear to come from / reply to the organizer identity (e.g., attendee email `from: ${organizer.name} <...>` and `replyTo: organizer.email`; organizer email `replyTo: [organizer.email, ...attendees]`). This combination enables abuse (mass email sending) directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race between the dedup check and prisma createMany allows concurrent requests to insert duplicate attendee rows, and the dedup comparison is case-sensitive so 'User@X.com' vs 'user@x.com' produces duplicates; no DB unique constraint on (bookingId, email)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, deduplication is done in application code by reading `booking.attendees` and filtering with a case-sensitive comparison (`guest === attendee.email`) before `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. There is no normalization (e.g., lowercasing) and no transactional/atomic guard, so concurrent requests can both pass the check and attempt to insert the same email, and mixed-case variants like `User@x.com` vs `user@x.com` are treated as different. The diff also shows `createMany` without `skipDuplicates`, so the code itself does not prevent duplicates (or prevents them only if an unseen DB constraint exists).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failures are swallowed with console.log and the error object is discarded, so the mutation returns 'Guests added' success even when no guest was notified or ICS invite sent

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This means email/ICS notification failures are swallowed (error object discarded, no propagation), so the mutation reports success even if no notification was sent. However, the core mutation behavior (adding guests + updating calendar attendees) can still succeed, so this is more an error-handling/observability issue than a guaranteed functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Seated bookings: no capacity check before inserting attendees and no bookingSeat records are created, allowing overbooking and divergence from seats-flow logic

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation blindly appends new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without any check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` / capacity (those fields are only copied into `evt` later). For seated bookings this can increase attendee count beyond the intended seat limit. The diff also shows no creation/update of any seat-tracking records—only `attendees` are modified—so it risks diverging from any seats-based booking flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial-failure ordering: DB write happens before updateCalendarAttendees with no rollback, so a calendar failure persists guests but returns an error, and retrying hits the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' BAD_REQUEST because uniqueGuests.length is 0

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the Prisma update (`prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`) occurs before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. There is no transaction/rollback or compensating delete if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, so the mutation can fail while the DB still has the newly-created attendees. A subsequent retry will compute `uniqueGuests` as empty because those emails are now in `booking.attendees`, triggering `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid` (`if (uniqueGuests.length === 0) throw ...`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) throws a raw Prisma 500 error instead of a handled TRPCError when booking.userId is null

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined`, this will query `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma "record not found" exception that is not converted to a `TRPCError` (there is no try/catch around this call), resulting in an unhandled/500-style error path rather than a controlled TRPC error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No guard against adding guests to past events, since there is no startTime check, resulting in CONFIRMED invites being sent for meetings that already happened

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` there is no check comparing `booking.startTime`/`booking.endTime` against "now" before updating attendees and sending calendar/email updates. The code always builds a `CalendarEvent` (using `dayjs(booking.startTime).format()`) and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, whose templates generate an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"`. This does allow adding guests (and sending invites) for bookings in the past, but whether that is a true defect vs. an acceptable product behavior isn’t specified by the diff.
